# Acceptance Criteria

## Functional Criteria

- [ ] Given a valid complete user payload, when `POST /users` is called, then a user is persisted and the API returns `201 Created`.
- [ ] Given existing users, when `GET /users` is called, then the API returns all users in one unpaginated list without search parameters.
- [ ] Given an existing user ID and a valid complete payload, when `PUT /users/{id}` is called, then the user is updated and the API returns `200 OK`.
- [ ] Given a missing user ID, when `PUT /users/{id}` is called, then the API returns the existing error format with `404 Not Found`.
- [ ] Given a login or email already used by another user, when create or update is called, then the API returns the existing error format with `409 Conflict`.
- [ ] Given a password shorter than 7 characters, when create or update is called, then validation rejects the request with `400 Bad Request`.
- [ ] Given a password of at least 7 characters, when create or update is called, then no additional password restrictions are applied.
- [ ] Given missing name, login, email, or password, when create or complete update is called, then validation rejects the request with `400 Bad Request`.
- [ ] Given any user response, when it is serialized, then the password is not included.
- [ ] Given a request to delete a user, when the API contract is inspected or the endpoint is called, then no user DELETE operation is available.

## API Criteria

- [ ] Request and response payloads match the documented `/users` contract and use the fields name, login, email, and write-only password as defined.
- [ ] Validation errors return the expected status and existing error body.
- [ ] Duplicate login and email values are exact, case-sensitive uniqueness conflicts and return `409 Conflict`.
- [ ] GET, POST, and PUT user operations are accessible without authentication.
- [ ] The OpenAPI contract defines no pagination, search, roles, authentication requirement, or DELETE operation for users.
- [ ] POST returns `201`; GET and PUT return `200`.
- [ ] Backward compatibility impact is documented: existing game endpoints and behavior remain unchanged.

## Architecture Criteria

- [ ] Controllers/delegates remain thin and delegate to application services.
- [ ] Domain code remains independent from adapters and infrastructure.
- [ ] REST DTOs, mappers, application services, domain models, and persistence adapters stay in their current layers.
- [ ] Generated OpenAPI sources are regenerated by Maven and are not manually edited.
- [ ] Login and email uniqueness is enforced both by application checks and database constraints.
- [ ] PostgreSQL remains the normal runtime database and H2 remains the test database.

## Test And Validation Criteria

- [ ] Focused service tests cover list, create, complete update, duplicate fields, missing users, and password boundary validation.
- [ ] Integration tests cover successful GET/POST/PUT, validation errors, `404`, `409`, unauthenticated access, and password omission from responses.
- [ ] Persistence tests cover storage, retrieval, listing, and duplicate constraints using H2.
- [ ] Relevant architecture tests pass.
- [ ] OpenAPI generation succeeds from a clean Maven build.
- [ ] Existing game tests continue to pass.
- [ ] Documentation is updated if endpoint documentation is present in `README.md`.
